examples.ko: 새 부츠가 발에 맞지 않아서 뒤꿈치에 물집이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The new boots didn't fit, so I got a blister on my heel.
My heels crack in winter, so I put on cream.

examples.ko: 아기가 깰까 봐 뒤꿈치를 들고 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked on tiptoe so the baby wouldn't wake up.
The heels of my sneakers are all worn out.
There is a hole in the heel of my sock.
My heel hurt while running, so I went to the hospital.

explain: 몸에서는 '발뒤꿈치'라고 해요. 신발이나 양말의 뒤쪽 부분도 '뒤꿈치'라고 부를 수 있어요. '뒤꿈치를 들다'는 발끝으로 서서 조용히 걷거나 키를 높일 때 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: My heels are very dry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 부분을 말할 때는 '발'을 붙여 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the body part, adding 발 makes it clear.

phrases.example: 아기가 깰까 봐 뒤꿈치를 들고 걸었어요.
phrases.en: I walked on tiptoe so the baby wouldn't wake up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 걷거나 키를 높일 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for walking quietly or reaching higher.

phrases.en: I walked a long way, so my heel hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아픈 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where your body hurts.

explain_en: For the body part the full word is '발뒤꿈치'. The back part of a shoe or sock can also be called '뒤꿈치'. '뒤꿈치를 들다' is used when you stand or walk quietly on your toes or try to look taller.

examples.en: The lipstick I just bought is really pretty.
I want to buy a red lipstick.
I always keep a lipstick in my bag.
A lipstick mark was left on the cup.
My younger sister wrote on the mirror with lipstick.

examples.ko: 저는 립스틱도 잘 안 바르는 편이에요.
examples.en: I rarely put on lipstick either.

explain: '립스틱을 바르다', '립스틱이 묻다'처럼 써요. 입술에 바르는 다른 제품으로 '립밤', '립글로스'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I put on lipstick before going out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입술에 바를 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for putting it on your lips.

phrases.en: There is lipstick on the cup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 립스틱이 다른 곳에 남았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when lipstick is left on something.

phrases.en: Red lipstick suits you well today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 앞에 붙여 어떤 립스틱인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting a color first tells which lipstick.

explain_en: It is used as '립스틱을 바르다' (apply) and '립스틱이 묻다' (get smeared). Other lip products include '립밤' and '립글로스'.

en: to want to go to the toilet; to feel an urge to urinate

examples.ko: 영화 보는 중에 갑자기 오줌이 마려워졌어요.
examples.en: In the middle of the movie I suddenly needed to pee.

examples.ko: 아이가 오줌이 마렵다고 해서 차를 세웠어요.
examples.en: The child said he needed to pee, so I pulled the car over.
I drank a lot of coffee, so I keep needing to go.
I really need to pee. Where is the restroom?

examples.ko: 긴 버스 안에서 갑자기 마려우면 어떡해요?
examples.en: What do you do if you suddenly need to go on a long bus ride?

examples.ko: 어제는 시험 보는 내내 마려워서 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I needed to go the whole time during the test, so it was hard.

explain: '오줌이 마렵다'처럼 꼭 '이/가'와 함께 써요. 어른이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 '화장실에 가고 싶어요'라고 돌려 말하는 경우가 많아요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '마려워요', '마려운', '마려우면'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: I have needed to pee since a while ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용이고 'ㅂ'이 '워'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, where ㅂ changes to 워.

phrases.en: The child who needed to pee ran to the bathroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form that describes the noun after it.

phrases.en: If you need to pee, don't hold it, just tell me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-면'을 붙여 조건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: -면 makes a condition: 'if you need to'.

explain_en: It is always used with '이/가', as in '오줌이 마렵다'. With adults or people you just met, people often say '화장실에 가고 싶어요' instead to be more indirect. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '마려워요', '마려운' and '마려우면'.

examples.en: Take the medicine three times a day.
I take vitamins every morning.
I took cold medicine and now I'm sleepy.

examples.ko: 복용하는 약이 있으면 의사에게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you are taking any medicine, tell the doctor.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹고 나서 복용하면 속이 편해요.
examples.en: If you take it after a meal, your stomach feels better.

examples.ko: 아이는 약을 혼자 복용할 수 없어요.
examples.en: A child can't take medicine alone.

explain: 복용하다는 약이나 영양제를 먹는 걸 말해요. 일상에서는 '약을 먹다'라고 하고, 복용하다는 병원, 약국, 약 설명서에서 자주 보여요. 약이 아닌 음식에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I take my medicine after breakfast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 자연스러운 말이고, 복용하다보다 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural everyday phrase, softer than 복용하다.

phrases.example: 약 상자에서 복용 방법을 읽어 보세요.
phrases.en: Please read the directions for taking it on the medicine box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약 설명서나 병원에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen on medicine labels and at hospitals.

phrases.example: 이 약은 술을 마신 후에 복용하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Do not take this medicine after drinking alcohol.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약국이나 설명서에서 하지 말라고 안내할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in pharmacies and instructions to say not to do something.

explain_en: 복용하다 means to take medicine or supplements. In daily talk people say '약을 먹다'; 복용하다 is what you see at hospitals, pharmacies, and on package inserts. It is not used for ordinary food.

examples.en: The place where the bug bit me has swollen up red.

examples.ko: 라면을 먹고 자면 아침에 얼굴이 부어올라요.
examples.en: If I eat ramen and sleep, my face puffs up in the morning.
I sprained my ankle and it is gradually swelling up.
I cried so much that my eyes swelled up.
If the wound swells up, go to the hospital.
After I used an ice pack, the swollen area went down.

explain: '붓다'와 비슷하지만 '부어오르다'는 눈에 띄게 부풀어 오르는 느낌이 더 강해요. 얼굴이나 눈은 일상에서 그냥 '붓다'라고 말하는 경우도 많아요. '부어올라요, 부어오른'처럼 '붓다'의 활용을 따라가요.

phrases.en: My eyes are puffy because I went to bed late yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '부어오르다' 대신 그냥 '붓다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, people often just say 붓다 instead of 부어오르다.

phrases.en: I fell and my ankle swelled up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 곳이 눈에 띄게 커질 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when an injured spot visibly swells.

phrases.en: I put ice on it, so it did not swell up more.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부은 상태가 더 심해지지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the swelling did not get worse.

explain_en: It is similar to '붓다', but '부어오르다' sounds more like a clearly visible swelling. For the face or eyes, people often just say '붓다' in daily talk. It follows the conjugation of '붓다', as in '부어올라요' and '부어오른'.

examples.en: I bumped into the door and my little toe hurts.

examples.ko: 새 신발 때문에 새끼발가락에 물집이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The new shoes gave me a blister on my little toe.
I hurt my little toe and went to the hospital.
A hole appeared in the little-toe part of my sock.
The tip of my little toe is red and swollen.

examples.ko: 새끼발가락 쪽이 자꾸 쓸려서 밴드를 붙였어요.
examples.en: The little-toe side keeps rubbing, so I put on a bandage.

explain: 반의어처럼 쓰는 말은 '엄지발가락'이에요. 책상이나 문 모서리에 '새끼발가락을 찧다'라고 많이 말해요. 손에는 짝말인 '새끼손가락'이 있어요.

phrases.en: I banged my little toe on the corner of the bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모서리에 세게 부딪혔을 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for hitting the toe hard on a corner.

phrases.en: I hurt my little toe while exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 원인을 따로 말하지 않고 다쳤다는 사실만 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say it got hurt without describing how.

phrases.en: My little toe swelled up because of the high heels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발가락이 부어오른 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the toe is swollen.

explain_en: Its counterpart is '엄지발가락' (big toe). People often say '새끼발가락을 찧다' (stub your little toe) on a desk or door corner. The matching word for the hand is '새끼손가락'.

examples.en: My stomach was bad, so I went to the hospital.
I ate too much and my stomach hurts.

examples.ko: 매운 음식은 위장에 부담을 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: Spicy food can put a strain on your stomach.
I skipped breakfast for a stomach exam.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차가 위장을 편안하게 해 줘요.
examples.en: Warm tea settles your stomach.

examples.ko: 아침을 안 먹으면 위장이 비어서 속이 쓰려요.
examples.en: If I skip breakfast, my stomach is empty and it burns.

explain: 위만 말할 때는 '위', 소화 기관 전체를 말할 때는 '위장'이라고 해요. 말할 때는 '속이 안 좋아요'도 많이 써요. 소리가 같은 '위장'은 정체를 숨긴다는 뜻의 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 위장이 약해서 매운 음식을 못 먹어요.
phrases.en: My stomach is weak, so I can't eat spicy food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소화가 잘 안 되는 몸 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a body that digests poorly.

phrases.en: My stomach hurt, so I took stomach medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위와 장이 아플 때 먹는 약이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Medicine taken when the stomach or bowels hurt.

phrases.en: I will have a stomach exam at the hospital tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 소화 기관을 살펴보는 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a hospital check of the digestive system.

explain_en: For the stomach alone there is the shorter '위'; '위장' covers the digestive organs together. In speech, people also say '속이 안 좋아요' (my insides feel bad). A different word with the same sound, '위장' (disguise), means to hide one's identity.

en: to have one's hair cut; to have haircut

examples.ko: 아버지는 한 달에 한 번 이발하세요.
examples.en: My father gets a haircut once a month.
I am going to get a haircut on the weekend.
My hair was long, so I got a haircut yesterday.
After the haircut, I feel refreshed.
I have to get a haircut before graduation.
It hasn't been long since I got a haircut.

explain: '이발하다'와 '머리를 자르다'는 둘 다 머리카락을 자를 때 써요. 이발하는 곳은 '이발소'예요. 미용실에서는 보통 '머리 자르러 왔어요'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: My head feels cool after the haircut.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이발하다'와 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '이발하다' and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: My father often goes to the barber shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이발하는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where you get a haircut.

phrases.en: I feel good after getting a haircut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이발이 끝난 뒤를 말할 때 '-고 나서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-고 나서' to talk about after the haircut is done.

explain_en: Both '이발하다' and '머리를 자르다' are used for cutting hair. The place for it is an '이발소'. At a salon people usually say '머리 자르러 왔어요'.

examples.en: I put a face mask on in the evening.
I'll go buy a carton of milk.
I stick a straw into the juice carton and drink.
My skin is dry, so I do face masks often.
There are two packs of tofu in the fridge.

examples.ko: 즉석밥 팩 하나로 간단하게 한 끼를 먹었어요.
examples.en: I had a simple meal with one pack of instant rice.

explain: 한국에서 '팩'은 얼굴에 붙이는 '마스크 팩'을 가장 많이 가리켜요. 우유나 주스 같은 종이 용기는 '우유팩'처럼 불러요. 세는 말로도 써서 '두 팩'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I put on a face mask before bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴에 붙이는 팩을 분명하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to clearly mean the sheet-type face pack.

phrases.example: 다 마신 우유 팩은 씻어서 버려요.
phrases.en: I rinse the empty milk carton before throwing it away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우유나 주스를 담는 종이 용기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the paper container for milk or juice.

phrases.en: I bought two packs of juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이 용기에 든 것을 셀 때 숫자 뒤에 '팩'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach '팩' after a number to count things in cartons or packs.

explain_en: In Korea, 팩 most often means a face mask pack. Paper cartons for milk or juice are called things like 우유팩. It also works as a counter, as in '두 팩'.

en: to be recovered; to be revitalized; to get better

examples.en: I hope my injured leg recovers soon.
Health recovers slowly after surgery.
After resting a few days, my strength recovered a lot.

examples.ko: 경제가 회복될 때까지 조금 기다려 봐요.
examples.en: Let's wait a bit until the economy recovers.
The speed of recovery differs from person to person.

examples.ko: 잠을 잘 자야 피로가 회복되고 기분도 좋아져요.
examples.en: You need good sleep for fatigue to go away and your mood to improve.

explain: '낫다'는 병이나 상처에 주로 쓰고, '회복되다'는 체력·건강·경제·관계처럼 나빠졌던 것이 원래대로 돌아올 때 넓게 써요. '체력을 회복하다'는 내가 되찾는 느낌이고, '체력이 회복되다'는 저절로 좋아지는 느낌이에요. '감기가 회복되다'보다 '감기가 낫다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My energy came back after a good sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지쳤던 몸의 힘이 저절로 돌아올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a tired body's strength returns on its own.

phrases.en: The economy is slowly recovering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나빴던 경제나 상황이 다시 좋아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a bad economy or situation improves again.

phrases.en: After resting a week, my body fully recovered.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전히'를 넣어 다 나았다고 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 완전히 stresses a full recovery.

explain_en: 낫다 is mainly for illness and wounds, while 회복되다 covers anything that got worse and returns to normal, such as stamina, health, the economy, or a relationship. 체력을 회복하다 feels like you win it back yourself, while 체력이 회복되다 feels like it happens on its own. For a cold, 감기가 낫다 sounds more natural than 감기가 회복되다.
